biggest_catch: Pay is hourly ($10-$12/hr) for a 12-hour Election Day, and judge appointments run through the county political party chairs.
catches: Election-period work only; Election Day is a 12+ hour day.
Hourly pay, not a flat day rate; total depends on hours worked.
Judges are appointed through county party chairs (political appointment process).
Must be a qualified voter of the precinct; cannot hold elective office, be a candidate, or be related to an opposed candidate.
Presiding judge must attend election school before serving.

c1.evidence: McLennan County official DocumentCenter PDF (mclennan.gov) — Election Worker Employment Opportunities.

c3.evidence: No fee to apply or serve.

eligibility: Qualified voter of the precinct; not holding elective public office; not a candidate in that election; not related within 2nd degree to an opposed candidate; not a campaign treasurer.
notes: Clerk appointments are made by the Presiding Judge; bilingual (Spanish) workers especially sought.
numeric_basis: payout: official $10-$12/hr x official 12-hr Election Day (7am-7pm); time: 720-min day + required presiding-judge election school (duration unstated, est 120-180 min)
payout_quote: The current pay for working as a Presiding Election Judge is $12.00 per hour, Alternate Judges are $12.00 per hour, and Election clerk is $10.00 per hour. The Presiding Judge will be present at the polling place during the official hours of voting (7:00 a. m. - 7:00 p.m.).
payout_value_note: $10-$12/hr by role x 12-hr Election Day (official 7am-7pm voting hours).

s1.note: Qualified voter of precinct; office/candidacy/relationship restrictions.

s6.note: Steps concrete: call elections office, party-chair appointment, election school, serve Election Day.

steps: Contact the McLennan County Elections Administration Department at (254) 757-5043 to be placed on the list of available workers.
Election judges are appointed by the county political party chairpersons for a one-year term; the Presiding Judge appoints clerks.
Presiding judges attend the required election school prior to serving.
Serve at the polling place on Election Day during voting hours (7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m.).
timing: Election Day per the county election calendar; presiding judge election school before serving.
